Overview

Abu Dhabi as a Business Centre

Abu Dhabi is the largest of the seven emirates by area and the federal capital of the United Arab Emirates. The Statistics Centre Abu Dhabi reported an emirate population of 4,135,985 in 2024, of whom about 2.8 million live in the Abu Dhabi region, about one million in Al Ain and roughly 326,000 in Al Dhafra. Hydrocarbons remain central to the economy, but the emirate has invested heavily in finance, industry, logistics, technology and real estate. Abu Dhabi Global Market, established by federal decree and open for business since October 2015, is a financial free zone on Al Maryah Island with its own common law based courts, registrar and financial regulator.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Abu Dhabi because of the scale of the capital that originates or is managed there. Sovereign and state-linked investors, energy and industrial groups, and the funds and family offices drawn to ADGM are frequent counterparties in cross-border transactions, joint ventures and fund raisings. That raises recurring questions: whether an intermediary claiming access to a state-linked investor is genuine, who controls an ADGM holding structure, how a contractor in the energy supply chain has performed elsewhere, and whether a counterparty in a dispute holds assets that can be reached. Each question depends on knowing whether the entity sits onshore, in ADGM or in another free zone.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Abu Dhabi

01

Sovereign-linked intermediary verification

Testing claims by advisers, agents and introducers that they represent or can secure capital from Abu Dhabi state-linked investors, by checking published mandates, corporate filings, litigation records and reputation through lawful sources, before a client pays fees or shares confidential information.

02

ADGM structure and ownership research

Identifying the officers, shareholders and related entities of companies, funds and foundations registered in ADGM, using the public register and other lawful sources, and explaining clearly where beneficial ownership cannot be confirmed because ADGM does not publish its record of beneficial owners.

03

Energy and industrial supply chain diligence

Reviewing contractors, subcontractors and agents bidding into oil, gas, petrochemical and industrial projects, including ownership, related parties, sanctions exposure, adverse media and track record on comparable projects in the Gulf and elsewhere. Findings distinguish verified facts from unconfirmed allegations.

04

Asset tracing for award enforcement

Locating company interests, property links and other assets in Abu Dhabi connected to a judgment or award debtor, so counsel can assess whether recognition through ADGM Courts or the onshore courts is worth pursuing and which entities and holdings to name in applications.

05

Senior hire and partner backgrounds

Verifying the career history, directorships and reputation of executives, fund managers and family office principals who have worked across the Gulf and international markets, reconciling CVs and regulatory statements against public records in each jurisdiction concerned.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Abu Dhabi

Onshore courts of Abu Dhabi

Onshore civil and commercial disputes in the emirate are heard by the local court system administered by the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, which proceeds in Arabic through courts of first instance, appeal and cassation. Court records and judgments are not generally open for third-party searching in the way some common law registries are, so litigation history is usually assembled from published decisions, media and counsel enquiries.

ADGM Courts and arbitration

ADGM Courts sit on Al Maryah Island and apply ADGM's own civil and commercial laws, built on common law principles, in English. They are one of ADGM's three independent authorities alongside the FSRA and the Registration Authority. The ADGM Arbitration Centre began full operations in October 2018 as a hearing facility open to parties whatever institution administers their dispute. Onshore, the Abu Dhabi International Arbitration Centre (arbitrateAD) is the emirate's main arbitral institution.

ADGM registry and beneficial ownership

The ADGM Registration Authority maintains the public register of ADGM companies, partnerships and foundations. Under the Beneficial Ownership and Control Regulations 2022, as amended several times since, entities must record beneficial owners holding 25 percent or more, or exercising control, and report changes within 15 days. ADGM states that its record of beneficial owners is not published for privacy reasons, and the Registrar may disclose it only in limited statutory circumstances or with consent.

Onshore licensing and other free zones

Businesses outside ADGM are licensed onshore by the emirate's economic development authorities or by one of Abu Dhabi's other free zones, each with its own licensing records and level of public disclosure. There is no single searchable register covering every Abu Dhabi entity, so the licensing authority must be identified before research begins. ADGM's jurisdiction has also been extended beyond Al Maryah Island to Al Reem Island, which affects where some newer entities are registered.

Financial regulation in ADGM

The Financial Services Regulatory Authority supervises banks, asset managers, insurers, virtual asset businesses and other firms operating in or from ADGM, and publishes its public register of authorised firms and enforcement notices. Those publications are a lawful starting point for checking whether an investment manager or adviser based in Abu Dhabi holds the permissions it claims. Onshore financial institutions fall under the federal Central Bank and Securities and Commodities Authority.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Abu Dhabi

TDSC handles Abu Dhabi matters from Nashville, with no presence in the emirate. Each engagement starts by establishing where the relevant entities are licensed, onshore, in ADGM or in another free zone, and which registers, regulatory publications and court sources lawfully cover them. Research draws on the ADGM public register and FSRA publications, published judgments, commercial databases and open sources read in Arabic and English. Where state-linked parties are involved, TDSC limits work to lawful public information and reports on what cannot be confirmed. Any local enquiries are scoped with UAE counsel and carried out by appropriately authorised local professionals; surveillance and recording are excluded. Personal data is handled with the federal and ADGM data protection regimes in mind.

TDSC has no office in Abu Dhabi. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Abu Dhabi: Frequently Asked Questions

How does ADGM differ from onshore Abu Dhabi for research purposes?

ADGM has its own registrar, financial regulator and English-language courts applying common law based rules, and it publishes a searchable register of entities and authorised firms. Onshore entities are licensed by emirate authorities and disputes go to Arabic-language local courts. TDSC identifies which system applies before deciding which records to review.

Can TDSC identify the beneficial owner of an ADGM company?

Not from the ADGM beneficial ownership record itself, which ADGM states is not published and is disclosed only in limited circumstances. TDSC works from the public register, filings, fund documents, regulatory notices, litigation and media to build an ownership picture, and states clearly where the ultimate owner remains unconfirmed.

How can a client test an intermediary who claims links to Abu Dhabi sovereign investors?

By checking the claim against what is lawfully public: the intermediary's corporate filings and regulatory status, published mandates or transactions, litigation, and reputation among parties who have dealt with them. TDSC does not contact state entities under pretext. Where doubt remains, clients are advised to seek confirmation directly from the investor through formal channels.

Which arbitration bodies are relevant in Abu Dhabi?

Contracts may refer disputes to the Abu Dhabi International Arbitration Centre (arbitrateAD), to ADGM-seated arbitration or to international institutions, and the ADGM Arbitration Centre provides hearing facilities for proceedings administered elsewhere. TDSC adapts research to the evidence the chosen tribunal and seat are likely to require; counsel advises on procedure.

Does federal UAE law still apply to matters in ADGM?

ADGM has its own civil and commercial laws, data protection regulations and courts, but federal criminal law, including the rules on privacy, recording and cybercrime, applies throughout the UAE. Investigative methods are therefore planned around both layers, and TDSC excludes surveillance, recording and pretext techniques in Abu Dhabi matters.
